brackets.note: Flat rate. The statute computes the tax at three percent on net income, with no separate schedule by filing status. Tax Foundation agrees.

earnedIncomeCredit.note: "five percent of the federal earned income tax credit" for tax years 2019 through 2030, refundable. It reverts to 3.5% in 2031.
earnedIncomeCredit.name: Louisiana earned income credit

standardDeduction.note: Read from the bulletin: $12,500 and $25,000 for 2025 times a 2.7% CPI-U multiplier. Head of household gets the joint amount. Tax Foundation shows $12,875 and $25,750 for 2026, which disagrees. The department's bulletin is used.

rules.note: Local tax flag is from Tax Foundation footnote (a), which lists no Louisiana local income taxes. The repeal of personal and dependent exemptions from 2025 is from PolicyEngine and matches Tax Foundation showing none. Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions. No employee payroll contribution: the US Department of Labor's comparison lists worker unemployment contributions only in Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania and disability insurance only in California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island, and no paid leave or similar program with an employee contribution was found for this state on 2026-11-12.
notes: Personal and dependent exemptions were repealed from tax year 2025 and replaced by the larger standard deduction.
The standard deduction is indexed each year by CPI-U, so the amount changes annually.
